name: Computer Graphics
description: Rendering images from 3D scenes: transforms, the GPU pipeline, shading and textures, ray tracing and animation.

nodes.name: Vectors & geometry
nodes.desc: Points, vectors, dot and cross products, lines and planes in 3D.
nodes.summary: You will be able to use points, vectors, dot and cross products, lines and planes to solve 3D geometry problems in graphics.

nodes.name: Transformations
nodes.desc: Translation, rotation and scaling with homogeneous coordinates and composition.
nodes.summary: You will be able to represent translation, rotation and scaling as matrices in homogeneous coordinates and compose them correctly.

nodes.name: Raster images
nodes.desc: Pixels, framebuffers, resolution and anti-aliasing.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how images are stored as pixels in framebuffers and reduce aliasing artefacts.

nodes.name: Colour & light
nodes.desc: RGB and colour spaces, gamma, HDR and how we perceive colour.
nodes.summary: You will be able to work with RGB and other colour spaces, apply gamma correction and explain HDR and colour perception.

nodes.name: Rasterisation
nodes.desc: Turning lines and triangles into pixels with barycentric interpolation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to convert lines and triangles into pixels and interpolate attributes with barycentric coordinates.

nodes.name: Cameras & projection
nodes.desc: View transforms, perspective and orthographic projection.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build view and projection matrices for perspective and orthographic cameras.
topics: Field of view and aspect ratio
Clip space and normalised device coordinates

nodes.name: The GPU pipeline
nodes.desc: Vertex processing, rasterisation, fragment processing and output merging on the GPU.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe each stage of the GPU pipeline from vertex processing to output merging.

nodes.name: Visibility
nodes.desc: Clipping, culling and the z-buffer.
nodes.summary: You will be able to determine visible surfaces using clipping, back-face and frustum culling and the z-buffer.

nodes.name: WebGL & OpenGL
nodes.desc: Buffers, shaders programs and draw calls in a graphics API.
nodes.summary: You will be able to draw geometry with WebGL or OpenGL using buffers, shader programs and draw calls.

nodes.name: Lighting models
nodes.desc: Ambient, diffuse and specular light with Phong and Blinn-Phong.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute ambient, diffuse and specular lighting with the Phong and Blinn-Phong models.

nodes.name: Shaders
nodes.desc: Writing vertex and fragment shaders for lighting and effects.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write vertex and fragment shaders in GLSL to implement lighting and visual effects.

nodes.name: Texture mapping
nodes.desc: UV coordinates, mipmapping, filtering and normal maps.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply textures with UV coordinates, filtering and mipmaps and add surface detail with normal maps.

nodes.name: Shadows
nodes.desc: Shadow mapping and its artefacts.
nodes.summary: You will be able to render shadows with shadow mapping and reduce its artefacts like acne and aliasing.
topics: Shadow map rendering from the light

nodes.name: Real-time renderer
nodes.desc: Build a renderer that loads meshes and draws lit, textured, shadowed scenes.
nodes.summary: You will build a real-time renderer that loads meshes and draws lit, textured and shadowed scenes.

nodes.name: Ray casting
nodes.desc: Generating rays and intersecting them with spheres, planes and triangles.
nodes.summary: You will be able to generate camera rays and compute intersections with spheres, planes and triangles.

nodes.name: BVHs & grids
nodes.desc: Acceleration structures that make ray tracing fast.
nodes.summary: You will be able to speed up ray tracing with bounding volume hierarchies and uniform grids.

nodes.name: Path tracing
nodes.desc: The rendering equation and Monte Carlo light transport.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain the rendering equation and estimate light transport with Monte Carlo path tracing.

nodes.name: PBR materials
nodes.desc: Physically based materials, microfacets and energy conservation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe physically based materials with microfacet models and energy conservation.

nodes.name: Ray tracer
nodes.desc: Write a path tracer that renders global illumination scenes.
nodes.summary: You will write a path tracer that renders scenes with global illumination using physically based materials.

nodes.name: Curves & surfaces
nodes.desc: Bezier curves, B-splines and subdivision surfaces.
nodes.summary: You will be able to construct Bezier curves, B-splines and subdivision surfaces and evaluate them.

nodes.name: Mesh processing
nodes.desc: Mesh data structures, normals, simplification and smoothing.
nodes.summary: You will be able to store and process meshes, compute normals, simplify them and smooth them.

nodes.name: Animation
nodes.desc: Keyframes, interpolation, quaternions and skeletal skinning.
nodes.summary: You will be able to animate objects with keyframes and interpolation, use quaternions for rotation and skin characters with skeletons.

nodes.name: Simulation
nodes.desc: Particles, cloth and rigid bodies with numerical integration.
nodes.summary: You will be able to simulate particles, cloth and rigid bodies using numerical integration methods.
